name: France
headline_status: Recreational cannabis is illegal in France, and medical cannabis is still limited to patients left over from a state trial while a permanent framework is prepared.
summary: Using cannabis in France is a criminal offence carrying up to one year in prison and a €3,750 fine, though since September 2020 police can instead issue a €200 on-the-spot fine that still goes on the criminal record. A state medical cannabis trial began on 26 March 2021 and stopped taking new patients in March 2024. Enrolled patients' access was extended past March 2026, while the decrees for a permanent medical programme were still being finalised in 2026.

penalties.value: Use is punishable by up to one year in prison and a €3,750 fine. Since 1 September 2020 police can issue a €200 fixed fine instead (€150 if paid within 15 days, €450 after 45 days), which is still recorded on the criminal record.

medical_since.value: Experimental programme only, launched 26 March 2021; no new patients admitted since 27 March 2024.

medical_program.value: Only patients already in the trial (just under 700 in April 2026) still receive reimbursed cannabis medicines, for conditions such as treatment-resistant neuropathic pain, drug-resistant epilepsy and some cancer symptoms; the health minister guaranteed continued access potentially until early 2027.

regulator.value: National Agency for the Safety of Medicines (ANSM) runs the medical trial; the High Authority for Health (HAS) is assessing reimbursement.

possession_limit.value: No legal amount. Cases over 100 g or repeat arrests go to criminal court rather than a fixed fine.

tourists.value: Visitors are subject to the same ban and penalties as residents, including the on-the-spot fine.

timeline.event: €200 on-the-spot fine for drug use introduced nationwide
Medical trial closes to new patients
President Macron announces plan to raise the drug-use fine from €200 to €500
Health minister guarantees continued access for trial patients, potentially until early 2027

pending.item: Permanent medical cannabis framework: draft decree, product specifications order and reimbursement rules, with a final HAS opinion expected in late 2026.
pending.status: Decrees not yet published as of April 2026; first prescriptions possible in 2027 if adopted in time.

pending.item: Government plan to raise the on-the-spot drug-use fine from €200 to €500.

faq.a: No. Use is a criminal offence, usually punished with a €200 on-the-spot fine but carrying up to a year in prison.

faq.q: Is medical cannabis legal in France?
faq.a: Only within a state trial that closed to new patients in 2024. A permanent programme is being prepared but was not in place as of 2026.

faq.q: Can tourists use cannabis in France?
faq.a: No. Visitors face the same penalties as residents.
